as_told.title: Questions to the Nine about Russian guerrilla code names

plain: In the 1970s a scientist named Andrija Puharich ran a research house called Lab Nine in Ossining, New York, where sessions were recorded on tape. Some of those sessions involved remote viewing, the claimed ability to see distant places or hidden things with the mind alone. A researcher named Greg says some of the tapes include questions like what time is best to remote view the Kremlin, the seat of the Soviet government, so they can get inside it. Another guest on the same episode, not named, says the questions included things like the code names used by Russian guerrilla soldiers. Both are researchers describing tapes they say they have heard, on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels. If true, the tapes would show these sessions were being used to spy on the Soviet Union.
